title: fix(app-shell,i18n): the boot screen says one honest line, in the user's language from the first paint (objectui#12187)
body:
Part of #12187
Clause-②: yes

This is item 1 of the three that triage comment 6118609734 separated: the boot copy, and no English before the locale. Items 2 (the chunk split on non-Studio routes) and 3 (one `sys_user_preference` read) stay open on #12187 and land as later pull requests under the same claim.

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat; implementing session `https://claude.ai/code/session_016djJF12Qt14ejKR5Vjt4sK`.

## What changes

- `LoadingScreen` (`@object-ui/app-shell`) draws the product name, one line and a spinner. The three steps it advanced on a 1200 ms `setInterval` are gone, and so is the "Setting up a new environment can take a few moments." hint. The error and retry block is unchanged.
- The one line is `console.initializing` with new copy in all ten packs: en "Opening your console…", zh 「正在打开你的控制台…」, and a translation in each of the other eight packs, in the register of its old value.
- `console.loadingSteps.connecting`, `console.loadingSteps.loadingConfig`, `console.loadingSteps.preparingWorkspace` and `console.loadingHint` are retired from all ten packs at once. There is no alias and no second spelling.
- The screen takes its language from the `I18nProvider` (`useObjectTranslation().language`). It reads the line off that language's resident built-in catalogue. While that catalogue is not resident, the line is left out (product name and spinner only). It is never shown in English.

## H1: the steps were cosmetic (confirmed)

`currentStep` was component state, advanced only by the timer. Nothing outside `LoadingScreen` read it or the step list. Outside the packs, `git grep` for `loadingSteps` and `loadingHint` finds only `LoadingScreen` and the three tests updated below.

## H2: where the English came from (measured)

The English came from the html element's `lang` attribute. Catalogue residency was not the cause.

- `getStartupStrings()` read `document.documentElement.lang` before `navigator.language`. `apps/console/index.html` ships `lang="en"`. The `I18nProvider` writes the attribute in a passive `useEffect`, and that runs after its children's first render.
- I measured the pre-fix component in jsdom, under the real `I18nProvider`, with a `zh-CN` browser, `lang="en"` and the zh catalogue resident. A sibling's layout effect recorded the first commit, before any passive effect ran:

| moment | html `lang` | splash text |
|---|---|---|
| first commit | `en` | ObjectOS, "Initializing application…", the three English steps, the English hint |
| after the provider's effect | `zh` | unchanged: English |
| t = 1199 ms | `zh` | unchanged: English |
| t = 1200 ms (first step tick) | `zh` | Chinese |

  So the step timer was the only thing that re-rendered the screen. A zh-CN user saw English for up to 1.2 s on every full page load, not only on cold ones.
- Residency is not the console's cause: `main.tsx` awaits `preloadBootstrapLocale()` before `createRoot().render()`. On this branch's production build in Chromium, the zh catalogue chunk's `responseEnd` was 1078 ms and the splash's first commit came at about 1118 ms.
- The fix reads the provider's language, which its state holds from its first render, so the attribute's timing no longer matters. The residency case is still covered: the line stays absent until the catalogue lands. The store write that lands it re-renders the screen, because `useObjectTranslation` binds store `added` events.
- The provider is unchanged. Writing the attribute during render would move a DOM side effect into render for every host. objectui#2871 already moved `containers.tsx` off the attribute and onto the provider's language, for the same desync.
- The old note in this file was "do not use useObjectTranslation here, it can suspend". The provider's instance comes from `createI18n`, which sets `react.useSuspense: false` for exactly that boot suspension, and the `Spinner` the screen renders calls the same hook. The objectui#7479 rule stands: no pack is imported back in (`check:eager-locale-catalogues` is green below).

## H3: a new value of `console.initializing`, no key added

`RedirectWithSplash` renders the same `LoadingScreen`, so that the handoff paints an unchanged screen (objectui#6378). It is the same boot face. These are the readers of `console.initializing`:
- `LoadingScreen`, as a property read off the pack;
- `RedirectWithSplash.test.tsx`, which asserts the string (updated);
- `ApiConsolePage.requestPreset-10591.test.tsx`, which reads `en.console.initializing` and works with any value;
- `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`, which needs the ellipsis glyph (every new value ends in it);
- `ar-participle-orthography-6610.test.ts`, which pins the Arabic form. The new ar value, 「جارٍ فتح وحدة التحكم…」, keeps the converged participle followed by an indefinite maṣdar heading an iḍāfa;
- `dead-key-batch-retired-4730.test.ts`, which checks the key is present in every pack.

## H4: the retired keys are in all ten packs

`packages/i18n/src/locales/` holds ten packs (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh). All ten carried all four keys, and all ten drop them. The pins now hold what remains:
- `ar-participle-orthography-6610`: the converged list keeps its five surviving rows (the three step rows left with their keys). The pack-wide rule is unchanged.
- `dead-key-batch-retired-4730`: the LoadingScreen blind-spot list keeps the five keys the screen still reads.
- `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` (a file-surface addition, see below): its positive control group named the three step keys as read by `LoadingScreen` through a property chain. It now names the four keys the file still reads that way. The negative control is unchanged.

## H5: the pre-JS splash carries no text

`#boot-splash` in `apps/console/index.html` is markup only, and `apps/console/src/__tests__/bootSplash.test.ts` ("ships no user-facing copy") pins that. I left it as it is.

## Locale evidence

These come from Chromium against this branch's production build (`vite build`, then `vite preview`), with a cold context per locale. `/api/v1/auth/get-session` was held so the splash stays on screen, and every other `/api` request was refused. A MutationObserver recorded the first commit that put text in `#root`.

| browser locale | html `lang` at first commit | splash text at first commit | at 2.5 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| zh-CN | `en` | ObjectOS / 正在打开你的控制台… | `lang` = `zh`, same text |
| en-US | `en` | ObjectOS / Opening your console… | same text |

Both show one line, no steps and no "new environment", and the first paint on a zh-CN cold context is not English. The run also saved one screenshot per locale. The REST channel cannot attach images, so the dispatch seat holds them.

## Tests and gates, at `0366b47`

- Targeted vitest at HEAD `0366b47`: `LoadingScreen.bootCopy-12187.test.tsx` (new, 5 tests), `RedirectWithSplash.test.tsx`, `ar-participle-orthography-6610.test.ts`, `dead-key-batch-retired-4730.test.ts` and `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts`: 5 files, 153 tests passed.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` at HEAD `0366b47` passed. `@object-ui/i18n` `type-check` passed on the first commit; its sources have not changed since.
- `packages/i18n/` whole suite, plus the dead-keys and en-drift script tests and `ApiConsolePage.requestPreset-10591.test.tsx`: 86 files, 1519 passed, 13 skipped.
- Boot-path batch (34 files): every app-shell `chrome/` test, every boot-path test that mocks `@object-ui/i18n` while rendering the real `LoadingScreen`, `MePermissionsProvider.retry.test.tsx` and `bootSplash.test.ts`. All 34 files and 279 tests passed.
- Build: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --filter=@object-ui/i18n` (28 tasks) and the console `vite build` both passed.
- `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift` ("Every changed en value was followed by all nine translation packs"), `check:i18n-dead-keys` (report), `check:eager-locale-catalogues` ("Exactly one locale catalogue is eager — `en`"), `check:eager-closure`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` and `check:doc-fences`: all exit 0.
- ESLint on the 17 changed source files (`--no-inline-config`, JSON format): 17 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. This narrowing is a measurement, not a skip. The config has no type-aware linting and no custom rule reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide scan is left to CI.

## Reverse verification and ablations

Each was a one-time mutation, landed through `ablation-replace` (anchor hit, blob changed), restored to the HEAD blob, with an empty `git diff HEAD` afterwards.
- `LoadingScreen` reads `document.documentElement.lang` again: 3 red, 2 green, as predicted. The red ones are the zh first-commit pin, the not-resident pin and the error-block pin.
- An `en` fallback for the line: only the not-resident pin goes red.
- The empty-language guard removed, over the 21 boot-path files that mock `@object-ui/i18n`: 10 files and 53 tests fail with a `TypeError`, because their `useObjectTranslation` doubles return no `language`. The guard is what keeps them green.
- Type direction: a reference to `en.console.loadingSteps` added to `LoadingScreen` gives TS2339 under `tsc`, so app-shell reads the rebuilt i18n typings. A `tsc --listFiles` run of `tsconfig.test.json` includes both changed app-shell test files. My first try at this mutation was a no-op: the replacement text contained the anchor, and the tool refused it. The second try used a different replacement.

## Published shape

`TranslationKeys` (the type of `en`) loses `console.loadingSteps` and `console.loadingHint`, and the value type of `console.initializing` changes. So the published shape does narrow, as the claim's `Clause-②: yes` reads. The changeset is `minor` for both packages, with a breaking note that maps each retired key to its replacement (none: the boot screen shows no steps, no hint).

## File surface

There is one file outside the claim's surface: `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts`. Its "both control groups … measured on THIS repository" block builds the three `console.loadingSteps.*` keys from segments. That is why a grep for the dotted keys did not find it. It asserts that `LoadingScreen` reads them, which this change ends. The edit drops those three rows and keeps the rule, the same treatment as the two i18n pins in the surface.

## Acceptance notes

- The comment in `apps/console/index.html` still says `LoadingScreen` "owns the init screen's ten-language step copy". H5 found the splash is markup only, so I left the file alone. The word "step" is now stale.
- `packages/i18n/README.md` ("Built-in locales") says `en` is "the synchronous dictionary the app-shell splash renders from before i18n is usable". The splash now renders from the active resident pack and keeps `en` only as the error block's per-field fallback. I did not edit it (outside the surface).
- The `scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` header bullet for `LoadingScreen` says it "deliberately does not call `useObjectTranslation` (its own comment says so)". That half is no longer true. The bullet's operative claim still holds: it reads its pack subtree through a local binding, so it is covered by design.
- `ConditionalAuthWrapper.tsx` keeps its own note that `useObjectTranslation` "suspends on first render". That note is about that file and was not touched. For instances built by `createI18n` the premise no longer holds.
- Ten boot-path test files mock `useObjectTranslation` without a `language`. `LoadingScreen` treats an empty language as no catalogue, and that is what keeps them green (measured above). Giving those doubles `language: 'en'` would let that branch go. It is not done here.
- On a host that does not preload, the `Spinner`'s accessible name (`common.loading`) goes through `t()`, so a screen reader hears the `en` fallback until the catalogue lands. Visible text is unaffected.
